question: How does Catholic ecclesiology use Isaiah 22:20-22 (Eliakim and the key of David) to support Petrine authority?

choices.A: It shows the OT pattern of a prime-ministerial 'steward' office with binding authority — a type that Christ fulfills by giving Peter the keys of the kingdom
choices.B: It proves Peter was a descendant of King David and therefore the rightful religious ruler
choices.C: It is only a poetic reference with no structural application to Church governance
choices.D: It shows the keys represent personal salvation, not institutional authority

teaching.title: Keys of the Kingdom — Isaian Background
teaching.body: In Isaiah 22, God appoints Eliakim as palace steward over the house of David, giving him 'the key of the house of David' — he will 'open and none shall shut.' Jesus echoes this language exactly in Matthew 16:19 when giving Peter 'the keys of the kingdom of heaven.' The typological argument is that just as the Davidic kingdom had a chief steward with binding authority (an office that continued from one person to the next), so Christ's kingdom has a Petrine steward whose authority continues through successors.
